program.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Program
program.blurb: Understand the FDE role, follow a month-by-month plan, build the right projects and walk into every interview round prepared.
program.credit: Career roadmap and interview breakdown adapted from the FDE Complete Career Roadmap 2026 by @hemant_careerbytes. The 6-month plan is from your own FDE_6_Month_Roadmap document.

overview.what: A Forward Deployed Engineer works directly with the client in the field. Instead of building a generic product from the company office, you go into the client's real environment and solve their specific problem. Palantir popularised the role, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Scale AI and many enterprise SaaS companies now hire for it. Think of it as a hybrid: part software engineer, part consultant, part product person.
daily: Visit the client site or join remote calls to understand their real problem
Analyse the client's data, systems and workflows
Build fast prototypes - sometimes in a single day
Write backend APIs, data pipelines and integrations
Give the product team real-world feedback so the product improves
Demo to client stakeholders and answer their questions

why.title: High impact
why.text: Your code directly solves a real client's production problem, so the feedback loop is very fast.

why.title: High pay
why.text: FDE roles usually pay top-tier packages because the hybrid skill set is rare.

why.title: Fast growth
why.text: Client-facing, business and technical skills all grow together.

why.title: Diverse exposure
why.text: Every client is a new domain: healthcare, defence, finance, logistics and more.

why.title: Career flexibility
why.text: Paths open up to Product Manager, Solutions Architect, Founder or Engineering Manager.

companies: Indian startups hiring as "Deployment Engineer" / "Implementation Engineer"

beginnerPath.title: Beginner path: 12 months
beginnerPath.intro: For people starting from zero. If you already program, skip Phase 1 and start at Phase 2.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.goal: Write small automation scripts and simple CRUD apps.
items: Python: variables, loops, functions, OOP
Data structures and basic algorithms (arrays, dictionaries, sorting basics)
Git & GitHub: repo, commit, push, pull, branching
SQL basics: SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, subqueries

phases.title: Backend + APIs
phases.goal: Build a full backend service that connects to a database and exposes APIs.
items: Build REST APIs with FastAPI or Flask (Python) or Express (Node.js)
Authentication basics: JWT, OAuth concepts
Test APIs with Postman
Work with a relational database (PostgreSQL)

phases.title: Cloud & Deployment
phases.goal: Deploy your project live on the cloud.
items: AWS/GCP basics: EC2/Compute, S3/Storage, IAM roles
Docker: containerise your backend app
Basic CI/CD: auto-deploy with GitHub Actions
Kubernetes basics (concepts and kubectl commands)

phases.title: Data Engineering & AI Basics
phases.goal: Build a mini AI-powered project that uses a data pipeline and an LLM API together.
items: ETL pipelines with Airflow or simple Python scripts
Data warehousing concepts: Snowflake / BigQuery basics
LLM APIs: build a small AI feature with the OpenAI or Claude API (chatbot, summariser)
Vector database basics (Pinecone / Chroma) and RAG

phases.title: Client-Facing Skills & Real Projects
phases.goal: Prepare one end-to-end case study: problem, solution and demo.
items: Practise mock client scenarios: write the problem in a document, then design the solution
Presentation skills: explain a project in a 5-minute demo
Read case studies: look up Palantir and Databricks FDE case studies
Connect with FDEs on LinkedIn and learn their career paths

phases.title: Applications & Interview Prep
items: Write a resume with projects and impact metrics (use numbers)
Polish your GitHub portfolio with good README files
Do mock interviews: coding, system design, behavioural
Find referrals by talking to current FDEs on LinkedIn
Apply: Palantir, Databricks, Scale AI and local enterprise SaaS companies

projects.intro: Recruiters want to see real problem-solving, not tutorial copies. In every README write the problem, the solution you built, and the impact (time saved, accuracy improved...). That is exactly the thinking an FDE interview tests.

items.title: Client Onboarding Automation Tool
items.text: Take a new client's CSV/Excel data and automatically clean and load it into a database (ETL + validation).

items.title: Internal Support Chatbot
items.text: A RAG chatbot over company documentation that answers employee queries (LLM API + vector DB).

items.title: Real-time Dashboard
items.text: Take any public API (weather, stocks, sports) and build a live dashboard with filters and alerts.

items.title: Multi-tenant SaaS Mini App
items.text: A small SaaS-style app where several 'clients' each see only their own data (multi-tenancy).

items.title: API Integration Hub
items.text: Combine two or three third-party APIs (payments, email, maps) into one unified API.

interview.intro: FDE interviews differ from normal software interviews: companies test communication, problem-solving speed and client-handling as well as coding. Expect 4 to 6 rounds, depending on the company (Palantir-style hiring).

rounds.name: Resume / application screening
details: A recruiter reviews your resume and portfolio.
They look for projects, impact metrics and signals of both coding and communication.
LinkedIn recommendations and GitHub activity help at this stage.

rounds.name: Recruiter / HR call
details: They learn your background and experience.
Expect: why are you interested in the FDE role?
Logistics: location, readiness to travel, notice period.
Salary expectations are discussed.

rounds.name: Technical / coding
details: A medium-level data structures and algorithms problem (LeetCode easy-medium).
Sometimes practical coding: "clean this dataset and produce this output".
A SQL query-writing round is possible.
Live coding: explaining your approach is essential - they watch your thinking process.

rounds.name: Case study / take-home
details: A real-world business problem, for example "here is client data - find insights".
You get 24-72 hours to complete it.
Tests coding and business thinking together.
You submit a presentation or document.

rounds.name: Case presentation / deep dive
details: Present your take-home to a panel.
They question your decisions, trade-offs and assumptions.
Communication and structured thinking matter most here.
Common question: why this approach and not another?

rounds.name: Behavioural / client-facing
details: Situational: "The client is aggressive and the deadline is impossible - what do you do?"
Examples of team collaboration.
Ambiguity: how do you work when requirements are unclear?
Travel and relocation readiness is confirmed.
Sometimes run by a senior FDE or Field Engineering Lead.

rounds.name: System design (optional)
details: Mostly for senior or mid-level roles.
Example: how would you design a scalable data pipeline or integration system?
Explain trade-offs: cost, scalability, latency.

rounds.name: Hiring manager
details: The final round: overall fit, long-term motivation and career goals.
The offer decision follows this round.

tips.title: Coding round
items: Solve 100-150 easy-medium LeetCode problems (arrays, strings, hashmaps, basic DP).
Practise SQL: joins, window functions, aggregations.
Practise explaining your approach out loud - avoid silent coding.
Do not forget edge cases.

tips.title: Case study round
items: Define the problem clearly before jumping to a solution.
Write down your assumptions and justify them.
Be data-driven: use numbers and metrics.
Keep slides simple and clean - do not over-complicate.
State trade-offs explicitly (time vs accuracy, cost vs scale).

tips.title: Behavioural round
items: Use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
Have real examples ready: team conflict, tight deadline, ambiguous requirement.
Prepare one strong client-facing example.
Be honest: a genuine "I didn't know, here is how I learned" story makes a good impression.

mistakes: Focusing only on coding and ignoring communication skills.
Presenting an over-complicated solution in the case study.
Jumping to a solution without understanding the client's real problem.
Not researching the company and its clients or domain.
Being unclear about travel or relocation flexibility.
interview.proTip: The panel mostly checks whether you are comfortable with ambiguity. In every answer, speak your thought process out loud: "First I will understand this, then check that, then design the solution." A structured approach impresses.

takeaways: FDE = technical skills + business understanding + communication - all three matter equally.
Showing impact in projects matters even more than the coding itself.
In interviews, structured thinking and clear communication score highest.
Consistency wins: practise a little every day.
